cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Declare Allegiance
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Will you wear my ribbon or Nina's for the chess club election? Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Keep us both as friends. Which one do you want as chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I wear yours today and hers tomorrow?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow's the vote. Tell me which ribbon you'll wear then; I'll happily lend you the other one today.

mechanism: A confidently organizes campaign support while accommodating friendship and daily ribbon preferences so B will still declare which candidate gets election-day backing.
confusable: Unlike merely wanting a decorative sign, A asks a choice between rival claimants; confidence depends on making that choice socially acceptable to B.
comparison: Friendship and election timing differ from a workshop hybrid plan and disputed meeting attribution.
seedUse: Use D58-b Nina/friendship/ribbon/vote-tomorrow with S02-b adapting participation terms.
